own_solution.law: Snell's law: theta2 = asin(n1 sin(theta1)/n2) = asin(sin 40 deg / 1.5)
assumptions: light passes from the first medium into the second

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: TE869 is claimed as the minimal pair of TB677 but differs in subject and reference direction (ceiling lamp / vertical vs incoming ray / normal) as well as attachment; the number and unit (11 deg) match and the authors disclose the difference in pair_note, so the claim is not false.

notes: Checked certified answers: base asin(0.642788/1.5 = 0.428525) = 25.374 deg; 46 deg: sin = 0.719340, /1.5 = 0.479560, asin = 28.657 deg; 51 deg: 0.777146/1.5 = 0.518097, asin = 31.205 deg; 54 deg: 0.809017/1.5 = 0.539345, asin = 32.639 deg. All match. No total internal reflection is possible going from n = 1 to n = 1.5, so all values are in domain. T63FD/TE795 form a clean minimal pair (same 11 deg, 'left there' vs 'tilted back again'). Numeral-free twins T5D6B and T6C87 match their numeric twins in wording. In pass 1 I labelled the tilt-and-return sentences C; the authors label them D. Since the final geometry carries no trace of the tilt, D is defensible and the answer is the same; this is a labelling difference, not a physics error.
